_comment: Superseded (pre-fix) dashboard panel bodies this product shipped and has since corrected in the honesty-hunt dashboards lane (2026-08-26). DashboardConfigMigrator re-bases an installed panel to the current shipped body ONLY when the installed panel (ignoring its enabled toggle) is byte-identical to one of these, i.e. the operator never edited it. An operator-edited panel matches nothing here and is left exactly as it is. enabled is deliberately omitted: it is the operator's toggle and is preserved across a re-base. The last two entries (alwayson/ag.redo_queue, alwayson/ag.send_queue) supersede the 2026-08-26 12:20 bodies rather than pre-fix ones: the retention lane (DECISIONS 2026-08-26 18:23 ruling 4) gave those two panels retainHistory and a description that no longer says 'not a retained historical trend', and an upgraded install would otherwise keep the old wording with retention never switched on. 2026-08-28, strings lane cluster 1 adds three more, and they are the AMPLIFIER trio: memory/pmemory.buffer_pool queried a memory-clerk type that exists on no SQL Server (CACHESTORE_BUFPOOL; the real one is MEMORYCLERK_SQLBUFFERPOOL), and livetempdb/livetempdb.used_mb and livetempdb/livetempdb.version_store_mb read the database-scoped sys.dm_db_file_space_usage unqualified while connected to master. All three returned NULL on every install (PROVED live on both NEW2022 and OLD2017), and the cached stat-card path turned that NULL into a confident 0 badged as fresh data (strings-r2-03, fixed in the same commit). The buffer-pool panel already had two entries here from the dashboards lane's prose fix; this third one covers an install that has already been re-based onto the 84beb1c body and so matches neither of those. 2026-08-28, strings lane cluster 3 adds six more: these are PROSE corrections, where the panel described one measurement while its query performed another, and an operator reading the old wording is being told something false whether or not the query changed. correlation/queryperf.top_queries and livewaits/waits.details each already appear above from the dashboards lane; those earlier entries hold the pre-dashboards-lane bodies, so an install re-based onto the 84beb1c body matched neither and needed the extra entry, exactly as pmemory.buffer_pool did. Two of the six changed more than prose: longqueries/longqueries.querytext stamped every row with getdate() instead of the row's own event_time (PROVED 2026-08-28: the same projection over a row dated 2020-01-02 reported 2026-08-28, a six-year error) and carried defaultDatabase master while its view lives in SQLWATCH (PROVED: Msg 208, Invalid object name, against master on NEW2022), so the query and the defaultDatabase are corrected alongside the wording. Registered here rather than shipped alone because none of these corrections would otherwise reach an install that already has the file.

panel.title: Redo Queue Trend
panel.description: Redo queue size over time. High values mean the secondary is falling behind.

query.sqlServer: SELECT GETDATE() AS [Time], ar.replica_server_name + ' / ' + DB_NAME(drs.database_id) AS [Series], CAST(drs.redo_queue_size AS BIGINT) AS [Value] FROM sys.dm_hadr_database_replica_states drs WITH (NOLOCK) INNER JOIN sys.availability_replicas ar WITH (NOLOCK) ON drs.replica_id = ar.replica_id WHERE drs.is_local = 0 ORDER BY [Value] DESC

panel.title: Send Queue Trend
panel.description: Log send queue size over time across all AG databases. Rising trends indicate network or throughput issues.

query.sqlServer: SELECT GETDATE() AS [Time], ar.replica_server_name + ' / ' + DB_NAME(drs.database_id) AS [Series], CAST(drs.log_send_queue_size AS BIGINT) AS [Value] FROM sys.dm_hadr_database_replica_states drs WITH (NOLOCK) INNER JOIN sys.availability_replicas ar WITH (NOLOCK) ON drs.replica_id = ar.replica_id WHERE drs.is_local = 0 ORDER BY [Value] DESC

panel.title: Checksum & Compression Detail
panel.description: Per-database breakdown of whether the most recent full backup used checksum and compression. Sorted by risk: no checksum and no compression first.

query.sqlServer: SELECT bs.database_name AS [Database], MAX(bs.backup_finish_date) AS [Last Full Backup], CASE MAX(CAST(bs.has_backup_checksums AS INT)) WHEN 1 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS [Checksum], CASE WHEN MAX(bs.compressed_backup_size) < MAX(bs.backup_size) THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS [Compressed], CAST(MAX(bs.backup_size)/1024.0/1024.0/1024.0 AS DECIMAL(10,2)) AS [Raw Size GB], CAST(MAX(bs.compressed_backup_size)/1024.0/1024.0/1024.0 AS DECIMAL(10,2)) AS [Compressed Size GB] FROM msdb.dbo.backupset bs WHERE bs.type = 'D' AND bs.backup_finish_date >= DATEADD(DAY,-7,GETDATE()) GROUP BY bs.database_name ORDER BY MAX(CAST(bs.has_backup_checksums AS INT)) ASC, bs.database_name

panel.title: Backups Without Compression
panel.description: Databases whose most recent full backup was taken without compression. Uncompressed backups consume significantly more storage and take longer to restore.

query.sqlServer: SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS FLOAT) AS [Value] FROM (SELECT bs.database_name, MAX(bs.backup_finish_date) AS last_backup FROM msdb.dbo.backupset bs WHERE bs.type = 'D' AND bs.backup_finish_date >= DATEADD(DAY,-7,GETDATE()) AND ISNULL(bs.compressed_backup_size, 0) >= bs.backup_size GROUP BY bs.database_name) x

panel.title: Top N Queries by Duration (Live)
panel.description: Real-time top 10 queries by average execution time — identify slow-running queries that need optimization.

query.sqlServer:
SELECT TOP 10
    qs.query_hash AS [Query Hash],
    qs.execution_count AS [Exec Count],
    CAST(qs.total_elapsed_time / 1000.0 / NULLIF(qs.execution_count,0) AS DECIMAL(14,1)) AS [Avg Duration (ms)],
    CAST(qs.min_elapsed_time / 1000.0 AS DECIMAL(14,1)) AS [Min (ms)],
    CAST(qs.max_elapsed_time / 1000.0 AS DECIMAL(14,1)) AS [Max (ms)],
    qs.last_execution_time AS [Last Exec],
    LEFT(st.[text], 100) AS [SQL Preview]
FROM sys.dm_exec_query_stats qs
CROSS APPLY sys.dm_exec_sql_text(qs.sql_handle) st
ORDER BY qs.total_elapsed_time DESC

panel.title: Wait Event Details
panel.description: Detailed wait statistics by wait type showing wait time, wait count, and percentage of total waits from SQLWATCH snapshots.

query.sqlServer:
SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ UNCOMMITTED; 
SELECT TOP 250
    h.report_time AS [Time],
    ISNULL(ws.wait_category, 'Other') AS [Category],
    mw.wait_type AS [Wait Type],
    SUM(d.wait_time_ms_delta) AS [Wait Time (ms)],
    SUM(d.waiting_tasks_count_delta) AS [Waiting Tasks],
    d.sql_instance
FROM dbo.sqlwatch_logger_perf_os_wait_stats d WITH (NOLOCK)
INNER JOIN dbo.sqlwatch_logger_snapshot_header h WITH (NOLOCK)
    ON h.snapshot_time = d.snapshot_time
    AND h.snapshot_type_id = d.snapshot_type_id
    AND h.sql_instance = d.sql_instance
LEFT JOIN dbo.vw_sqlwatch_meta_wait_stats_category ws WITH (NOLOCK)
    ON ws.sql_instance = d.sql_instance
    AND ws.wait_type_id = d.wait_type_id
LEFT JOIN dbo.sqlwatch_meta_wait_stats mw WITH (NOLOCK)
    ON mw.sql_instance = d.sql_instance
    AND mw.wait_type_id = d.wait_type_id
WHERE h.report_time BETWEEN @TimeFrom AND @TimeTo
    AND d.sql_instance IN (SELECT value FROM STRING_SPLIT(@SqlInstance, ','))
    AND d.wait_time_ms_delta > 0
GROUP BY h.report_time, ISNULL(ws.wait_category, 'Other'), mw.wait_type, d.sql_instance
ORDER BY h.report_time DESC, [Wait Time (ms)] DESC

panel.title: Wait Events by Category
panel.description: Wait time trends by category (CPU, I/O, Memory, Lock, Network) over time. Identifies shifting performance bottlenecks.

query.sqlServer:
SELECT
    h.report_time AS [Time],
    ISNULL(ws.wait_category, 'Other') AS [Series],
    SUM(d.wait_time_ms_delta) AS [Value]
FROM dbo.sqlwatch_logger_perf_os_wait_stats d WITH (NOLOCK)
INNER JOIN dbo.sqlwatch_logger_snapshot_header h WITH (NOLOCK)
    ON h.snapshot_time = d.snapshot_time
    AND h.snapshot_type_id = d.snapshot_type_id
    AND h.sql_instance = d.sql_instance
LEFT JOIN dbo.vw_sqlwatch_meta_wait_stats_category ws WITH (NOLOCK)
    ON ws.sql_instance = d.sql_instance
    AND ws.wait_type_id = d.wait_type_id
WHERE h.report_time BETWEEN @TimeFrom AND @TimeTo
    AND d.sql_instance IN (SELECT value FROM STRING_SPLIT(@SqlInstance, ','))

HAVING SUM(d.wait_time_ms_delta) > 0
ORDER BY h.report_time

panel.title: Slow I/O Requests (system_health)
panel.description: I/O requests that exceeded the slow I/O threshold captured by the system_health XEvent session.

query.sqlServer:
IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.server_event_sessions WHERE name = 'system_health')
BEGIN
  SELECT TOP 100
    xdr.value('(@timestamp)[1]','datetime2')           AS [Time],
    xdr.value('(data[@name="duration"]/value)[1]','bigint') / 1000 AS [Duration ms],
    DB_NAME(xdr.value('(data[@name="database_id"]/value)[1]','int')) AS [Database],
    xdr.value('(data[@name="file_id"]/value)[1]','int') AS [File ID],
    xdr.value('(data[@name="is_retry"]/value)[1]','bit') AS [Retry]
  FROM (
    SELECT CAST(target_data AS XML) AS target_data
    FROM sys.dm_xe_session_targets t
    JOIN sys.dm_xe_sessions s ON t.event_session_address = s.address
    WHERE s.name = 'system_health' AND t.target_name = 'ring_buffer'
  ) d
  CROSS APPLY target_data.nodes('//RingBufferTarget/event[@name=''io_request_slow'']') AS x(xdr)
  ORDER BY [Time] DESC
END
ELSE SELECT 'system_health XEvent session not running' AS [Info]

panel.title: Top N Queries by Duration (Live)
panel.description: Real-time top 10 queries by average execution time — identify slow-running queries that need optimization.

query.sqlServer:
SELECT TOP 10
    qs.query_hash AS [Query Hash],
    qs.execution_count AS [Exec Count],
    CAST(qs.total_elapsed_time / 1000.0 / NULLIF(qs.execution_count,0) AS DECIMAL(14,1)) AS [Avg Duration (ms)],
    CAST(qs.min_elapsed_time / 1000.0 AS DECIMAL(14,1)) AS [Min (ms)],
    CAST(qs.max_elapsed_time / 1000.0 AS DECIMAL(14,1)) AS [Max (ms)],
    qs.last_execution_time AS [Last Exec],
    LEFT(st.[text], 100) AS [SQL Preview]
FROM sys.dm_exec_query_stats qs
CROSS APPLY sys.dm_exec_sql_text(qs.sql_handle) st
ORDER BY qs.total_elapsed_time / NULLIF(qs.execution_count,0) DESC

panel.title: Query Performance Summary
panel.description: Aggregated query performance metrics — total queries, average/max duration, I/O stats, and blocking. BROKEN — StatCard mapper expects a Value column; query returns different shape. Disable until SQL or panel binding fixed.

query.sqlServer:
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS [Cached Query Plans],
    CAST(AVG(total_elapsed_time) / 1000.0 AS DECIMAL(14,1)) AS [Avg Duration (ms)],
    CAST(MAX(total_elapsed_time) / 1000.0 AS DECIMAL(14,1)) AS [Max Duration (ms)],
    CAST(SUM(total_logical_reads) * 8.0 / 1024 / 1024 AS DECIMAL(10,2)) AS [Logical Reads (GB)],
    CAST(SUM(total_physical_reads) * 8.0 / 1024 / 1024 AS DECIMAL(10,2)) AS [Physical Reads (GB)],
    CAST(SUM(total_logical_writes) * 8.0 / 1024 / 1024 AS DECIMAL(10,2)) AS [Logical Writes (GB)],
    CAST(AVG(total_worker_time) / 1000.0 AS DECIMAL(14,1)) AS [Avg CPU (ms)],
    CAST(MAX(total_worker_time) / 1000.0 AS DECIMAL(14,1)) AS [Max CPU (ms)],
    SUM(execution_count) AS [Total Executions]
FROM sys.dm_exec_query_stats

panel.title: Wait Event Details
panel.description: Detailed wait statistics by wait type showing wait time, wait count, and percentage of total waits from SQLWATCH snapshots.

query.sqlServer:
SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ UNCOMMITTED; 
SELECT TOP 250
    h.report_time AS [Time],
    ISNULL(ws.wait_category, 'Other') AS [Category],
    mw.wait_type AS [Wait Type],
    SUM(d.wait_time_ms_delta) AS [Wait Time (ms)],
    SUM(d.waiting_tasks_count_delta) AS [Waiting Tasks],
    d.sql_instance
FROM dbo.sqlwatch_logger_perf_os_wait_stats d WITH (NOLOCK)
INNER JOIN dbo.sqlwatch_logger_snapshot_header h WITH (NOLOCK)
    ON h.snapshot_time = d.snapshot_time
    AND h.snapshot_type_id = d.snapshot_type_id
    AND h.sql_instance = d.sql_instance
LEFT JOIN dbo.vw_sqlwatch_meta_wait_stats_category ws WITH (NOLOCK)
    ON ws.sql_instance = d.sql_instance
    AND ws.wait_type_id = d.wait_type_id
LEFT JOIN dbo.sqlwatch_meta_wait_stats mw WITH (NOLOCK)
    ON mw.sql_instance = d.sql_instance
    AND mw.wait_type_id = d.wait_type_id
WHERE h.report_time BETWEEN @TimeFrom AND @TimeTo
    AND d.sql_instance IN (SELECT value FROM STRING_SPLIT(@SqlInstance, ','))
    AND d.wait_time_ms_delta > 0
GROUP BY h.report_time, ISNULL(ws.wait_category, 'Other'), mw.wait_type, d.sql_instance
ORDER BY h.report_time DESC, [Wait Time (ms)] DESC

panel.title: Active Sessions
panel.description: Count of active user sessions from sys.dm_exec_sessions where is_user_process = 1.

query.sqlServer: SELECT TOP (@TopRows) s.spid AS Spid, DB_NAME(s.dbid) AS [Database], status AS Status, CAST(cpu AS BIGINT) AS Cpu, CAST(physical_io AS BIGINT) AS PhysicalIo, program_name AS ProgramName FROM sys.sysprocesses s WHERE s.spid > 50 AND program_name NOT LIKE '%SQLMonitorUI%' AND hostname <> '' AND program_name <> '' ORDER BY (ISNULL(cpu,0) + ISNULL(physical_io,0)) DESC

panel.title: Top Usage Queries
panel.description: Top active sessions by CPU, reads, or duration. Shows session_id, login, database, and current query text.

query.sqlServer:
SELECT
    TMP.Category,
    [Source],
    DB_NAME(st.dbid) [DB],
    TMP.[Total Elapsed Time in S],
    TMP.[Total Execution Count],
    TMP.[Total CPU Time in S],
    TMP.[Total Logical Reads],
    TMP.[Total Logical Writes],
    TMP.[Total CLR Time],
    TMP.[Number of Statements],
    TMP.[Last Execution Time],
    TMP.[Plan Handle],
    st.text AS [Query],
    qp.query_plan AS [Plan]
FROM (
    SELECT * FROM (
        SELECT TOP 15 'worst I/O' [Category],
            'Query' [Source],
            CAST(SUM(s.total_elapsed_time) / 1000000.0 AS DECIMAL(20, 2)) AS [Total Elapsed Time in S],
            SUM(s.execution_count) AS [Total Execution Count],
            CAST(SUM(s.total_worker_time) / 1000000.0 AS DECIMAL(20, 2)) AS [Total CPU Time in S],
            SUM(s.total_logical_reads) AS [Total Logical Reads],
            SUM(s.total_logical_writes) AS [Total Logical Writes],
            SUM(s.total_clr_time) AS [Total CLR Time],
            COUNT(1) AS [Number of Statements],
            MAX(s.last_execution_time) AS [Last Execution Time],
            s.plan_handle AS [Plan Handle]
        FROM sys.dm_exec_query_stats s WITH (NOLOCK)
        GROUP BY s.plan_handle ORDER BY SUM(s.total_logical_reads + s.total_logical_writes) DESC
    ) QS
    UNION ALL
        SELECT * FROM (
        SELECT TOP 15 'worst I/O' [Category],
            'Procedure' [Source],
            CAST(SUM(s.total_elapsed_time) / 1000000.0 AS DECIMAL(20, 2)) AS [Total Elapsed Time in S],
            SUM(s.execution_count) AS [Total Execution Count],
            CAST(SUM(s.total_worker_time) / 1000000.0 AS DECIMAL(20, 2)) AS [Total CPU Time in S],
            SUM(s.total_logical_reads) AS [Total Logical Reads],
            SUM(s.total_logical_writes) AS [Total Logical Writes],
            SUM(0e) AS [Total CLR Time],
            COUNT(1) AS [Number of Statements],
            MAX(s.last_execution_time) AS [Last Execution Time],
            s.plan_handle AS [Plan Handle]
        FROM sys.dm_exec_procedure_stats s WITH (NOLOCK)
        GROUP BY s.plan_handle ORDER BY SUM(s.total_logical_reads + s.total_logical_writes) DESC
    ) PS
) TMP
OUTER APPLY sys.dm_exec_sql_text(TMP.[Plan Handle]) AS st
OUTER APPLY sys.dm_exec_query_plan(TMP.[Plan Handle]) AS qp
ORDER BY Category, [Total Logical Reads] DESC
OPTION (MAXDOP 1)
